days.label: Sun 20 Dec
days.title: Arrival evening
days.summary: Land, check in, and keep it simple. The markets are closed on Sundays, so tonight is about an easy dinner and the Christmas lights.

slots.title: Check in, drop bags
slots.text: Use a luggage delivery counter at the airport if the flat isn't ready. Buy Suica or PASMO cards on your phones for trains.

slots.title: Marunouchi lights and Tokyo Station
slots.text: Tree-lined street lit in gold, a flat walk, right by Tokyo Station.

slots.title: Depachika dinner or Yūrakuchō under the tracks
slots.text: If everyone's tired, buy a picnic of bento, yakitori and sweets in the Daimaru or Tokyo Station food halls. If not, walk to the izakaya under the Yūrakuchō railway arches.
slots.alt: Easy: dinner delivered to the flat from the food halls.

days.label: Mon 21 Dec
days.title: Market day: Toyosu, Tsukiji, the river to Asakusa
days.summary: The early market day. The early crew sees the tuna auction; everyone meets for a big temple breakfast, grazes Tsukiji's side streets, then takes the river boat to old Asakusa and Kuramae.

slots.title: Taxi to Toyosu Market
slots.text: Trains don't run early enough. The upper gallery above the tuna auction opens at 5:00; the auction runs roughly 5:30–6:30.
slots.query: Toyosu Market Fish Wholesale Market Building

slots.title: Breakfast inside Toyosu
slots.text: The restaurant rows in the fish building serve sushi, kaisendon and fried seafood from dawn. Skip the counters with two-hour queues; the shorter lines next door use the same fish. Tonkatsu Yachiyo's fried horse mackerel and shrimp are cooked options.

slots.title: Everyone: 18-dish breakfast at Tsukiji Honganji
slots.text: An Indian-style Buddhist temple with a café serving a tray of 16 small dishes plus rice and miso. Almost all cooked, so good for her. Book online ahead.
slots.alt: The early crew can have coffee here and eat light.

slots.title: Graze the Tsukiji Outer Market
slots.text: Go for the back lanes: tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette) on a stick, grilled scallops, dashi and katsuobushi shops, Aritsugu for kitchen knives. It gets crowded by 10:30.

slots.title: Matcha in Hama-rikyū Gardens
slots.text: A tidal Edo-period garden with skyscrapers behind it. The teahouse on the pond serves matcha and a sweet. Flat paths.

slots.title: Water bus up the Sumida River to Asakusa
slots.text: About 35 minutes, seated, under a dozen bridges. Check the day's timetable; winter services are fewer.

slots.title: Asakusa: Sensō-ji and the side streets
slots.text: Lunch on the backstreets (tempura, soba, or monjayaki). Kappabashi kitchen street is 10 minutes' walk for plates, knives and plastic food samples.

slots.title: Rest at the flat
slots.text: A two-hour break before dinner.

slots.title: Kuramae: makers and river views
slots.text: Design shops, Kakimori (build your own notebook, mix your own ink), chocolate and coffee roasters. Walk to the river for Skytree lit up.

slots.title: Dinner: Monzen-nakachō izakaya
slots.text: A locals' drinking district by Tomioka Hachimangū shrine. Old-school izakaya, yakitori and oden. Book a table for six.

days.label: Tue 22 Dec
days.title: West side: shrines, fashion streets, Fuji at sunset
days.summary: Forest shrine in the morning, the best shopping streets at midday, then Mount Fuji's silhouette from Shibuya's rooftop at sunset and a noisy food-hall dinner.

slots.title: Meiji Jingū
slots.text: A long gravel walk through the forest to the shrine. Quiet before 9:30. Flat but about 1 km each way.
slots.alt: Easy: taxi to the north entrance, which is closer to the shrine.

slots.title: Harajuku backstreets and Cat Street
slots.text: Skip Takeshita Street. Cat Street and Ura-Harajuku have the streetwear and vintage shops.

slots.title: Omotesandō and Aoyama
slots.text: Architecture walk along the avenue. The Nezu Museum's garden is one of the best in Tokyo (closed Mondays, open today).

slots.title: Lunch in Oku-Shibuya (Tomigaya)
slots.text: The quiet neighbourhood behind Shibuya with small restaurants, Fuglen coffee, and Shibuya Publishing & Booksellers.

slots.title: Rest
slots.text: Back to the flat or a long coffee stop.

slots.title: Shibuya Sky at sunset
slots.text: Sunset is around 16:30 in late December. On clear winter days you can see Mount Fuji. Book the sunset slot as soon as tickets open; it sells out.
slots.alt: Free alternative: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observatory in Shinjuku.

slots.title: Shibuya Crossing and Miyashita Park
slots.text: Watch the crossing from above, then walk the rooftop park.

slots.title: Dinner: Shibuya Yokochō
slots.text: A long food hall of regional izakaya stalls under Miyashita Park. Loud and fun, with food from every region of Japan and space for six.
slots.alt: Quieter: Ebisu Yokochō, then the Christmas chandelier at Yebisu Garden Place.

days.label: Wed 23 Dec
days.title: Route A bonus: old Tokyo and a sumo hotpot
days.summary: Only in Route A. The oldest-feeling neighbourhood in the city, the national museum, and a chanko nabe dinner in the sumo district. In Routes B, C and D, this is your travel day to Fuji or Hakone.

slots.title: Yanaka, Nezu and Sendagi
slots.text: Wooden houses, temples, cats and craft shops. Nezu Shrine's red gate tunnel is a short, flat walk. Kayaba Coffee for egg sandwiches.

slots.title: Ueno Park and the Tokyo National Museum
slots.text: Japan's best collection of samurai armour, swords, kimono and Buddhist art. Plenty of benches. Closed Mondays; closed for year-end from 26 Dec.

slots.title: Ameyoko market street
slots.text: Loud, cheap market street under the tracks. Snacks, dried seafood, and year-end shopping crowds.

slots.title: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa: garden and coffee
slots.text: A stroll garden with stepping stones over the pond, then the coffee roasters that made this neighbourhood known. The Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo is nearby.

slots.title: Dinner: chanko nabe in Ryōgoku
slots.text: The sumo wrestlers' hotpot, cooked at the table. Filling, all cooked, and suited to a big group. The Edo-Tokyo Museum next door reopened in March 2026.

nights.name: Yūrakuchō / Shimbashi
nights.text: Office workers' izakaya built into the railway arches. Plastic stools, yakitori smoke, big tables. Very Tokyo, and easy to find space for six on a weekday.

nights.name: Shibuya Yokochō
nights.text: A food hall of regional izakaya stalls in Miyashita Park. Walk-in, space for groups, everyone can order different things.

nights.name: Ebisu Yokochō
nights.text: A covered alley of small stalls with a young crowd. Go as two groups and swap halfway.

nights.name: Monzen-nakachō
nights.text: A traditional drinking district by a shrine, few tourists. Best for a proper sit-down izakaya dinner.

nights.name: Kagurazaka
nights.text: Stone-paved lanes that used to be a geisha district, now full of small restaurants, some French-Japanese. Good for a quieter dinner with your parents.

nights.name: Omoide Yokochō and Golden Gai
nights.text: Tiny, famous and crowded. Many Golden Gai bars seat 6–8 people and charge a cover. A good late drink for the brothers after dinner.

nights.name: Sangenjaya (Sankaku Chitai)
nights.text: A triangle of back alleys packed with small bars, two stops from Shibuya. Almost no tourists.

nights.name: Tsukishima Monja Street
nights.fit: All six · cooked at the table
nights.text: Dozens of monjayaki restaurants. You cook a runny savoury pancake on a hot plate at your table. Fun for a group and fully cooked.

hoods.name: Asakusa & Kuramae
hoods.vibe: Tokyo's oldest temple, and next door, the craft and design district some call Tokyo's Brooklyn.
hoods.do: Sensō-ji at 7am before the crowds; river walk; Kappabashi kitchen street; Kakimori notebooks and ink.
hoods.eat: Tempura, soba, monjayaki; Hoppy Street stew stalls.
hoods.shop: Kuramae leather, stationery and ceramics; Kappabashi knives and plates.
hoods.forHer: Flat. Sensō-ji gets very crowded after 10:00.

hoods.name: Yanaka, Nezu & Sendagi
hoods.vibe: The area that survived the war and the earthquake. Temples, cats, small shops, old houses.
hoods.do: Yanaka Ginza shopping street, Yanaka Cemetery, Nezu Shrine, SCAI The Bathhouse gallery in an old bathhouse.
hoods.eat: Menchi-katsu croquettes on Yanaka Ginza; Kayaba Coffee.
hoods.shop: Handmade crafts, washi paper, tenugui towels.
hoods.forHer: Mostly flat, a few slopes.

hoods.name: Ueno
hoods.vibe: The big park with Tokyo's main museums and the loud Ameyoko market street.
hoods.do: Tokyo National Museum, National Museum of Western Art, Ueno Park, Shinobazu Pond.
hoods.eat: Ameyoko street food, izakaya under the tracks.
hoods.shop: Ameyoko for snacks and cheap sneakers.
hoods.forHer: Lots of benches; museums have lifts.

hoods.name: Tsukiji, Ginza & Nihonbashi
hoods.vibe: The outer fish market, the best department store food halls, and old merchant shops that have run for centuries.
hoods.do: Tsukiji Outer Market; Hama-rikyū garden; Nihonbashi bridge; Itoya stationery in Ginza.
hoods.eat: Depachika food halls at Mitsukoshi Nihonbashi and Ginza; Tsukiji tamagoyaki; tempura counters.
hoods.shop: Ginza Six, Dover Street Market Ginza, Uniqlo Ginza flagship, Itoya.
hoods.forHer: Very easy. Department stores have lifts, seating and good toilets.

hoods.name: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa
hoods.vibe: Quiet warehouse district turned coffee town, with a classic stroll garden and the contemporary art museum.
hoods.do: Kiyosumi Gardens, Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo, Fukagawa Edo Museum.
hoods.eat: Fukagawa-meshi (clams on rice), specialty coffee roasters.
hoods.shop: Small design and homeware shops.
hoods.forHer: Flat and calm.

hoods.name: Ryōgoku
hoods.vibe: Home of the sumo stadium and many sumo stables.
hoods.do: Edo-Tokyo Museum (reopened 31 Mar 2026), Kokugikan area, Sumida Hokusai Museum.
hoods.eat: Chanko nabe, the sumo hotpot.
hoods.shop: Sumo souvenirs.
hoods.forHer: Flat, museum has lifts.

hoods.name: Harajuku, Omotesandō & Aoyama
hoods.vibe: Tokyo's fashion streets, from streetwear on Cat Street to flagship buildings by famous architects on Omotesandō.
hoods.do: Meiji Jingū, Nezu Museum garden, Omotesandō architecture, weekend farmers' market at UNU.
hoods.eat: Small cafés on the Aoyama backstreets.
hoods.shop: Cat Street streetwear, Ura-Harajuku vintage, Omotesandō Hills, Aoyama designer stores.
hoods.forHer: Long walks; take taxis between areas.

hoods.name: Shibuya & Oku-Shibuya
hoods.vibe: The crossing, rooftop views, a big food hall at night, and a quiet backstreet neighbourhood with small labels and cafés.
hoods.do: Shibuya Sky at sunset, Miyashita Park, Shibuya Sakura Stage, Tomigaya backstreets.
hoods.eat: Shibuya Yokochō; Nonbei Yokochō; Tomigaya bistros.
hoods.shop: Tomigaya independent shops, Shibuya Parco (Nintendo, Pokémon, designer floors).
hoods.forHer: Crowded around the station; Tomigaya is quiet.

hoods.name: Daikanyama, Nakameguro & Ebisu
hoods.vibe: Tree-lined streets with Tokyo's best select shops, a canal lined with cafés, and a lively food alley in Ebisu.
hoods.do: Daikanyama T-Site bookstore, Log Road, Meguro River walk, Yebisu Garden Place winter illumination.
hoods.eat: Ebisu Yokochō; Nakameguro izakaya under the tracks.
hoods.shop: Select shops and Japanese labels in Daikanyama and Nakameguro.
hoods.forHer: Gentle walks, many cafés to stop in.

hoods.name: Shimokitazawa
hoods.vibe: Tokyo's vintage capital, rebuilt around new low-rise complexes along the old railway line.
hoods.do: Reload and Bonus Track complexes, Mikan Shimokita, small live-music venues.
hoods.eat: Soup curry, small bars.
hoods.shop: Dozens of vintage shops; independent labels at Reload.
hoods.forHer: Compact and flat.

hoods.name: Kōenji & Nakano
hoods.vibe: Where Tokyo's vintage and punk scene lives, plus Nakano Broadway, a mall of collectors' shops.
hoods.do: Kōenji backstreets; Nakano Broadway for anime, watches, cameras and toys.
hoods.eat: Standing bars and cheap izakaya in Kōenji.
hoods.shop: Kōenji vintage is cheaper than Shimokitazawa; Nakano for collectibles.
hoods.forHer: Flat.

hoods.name: Kichijōji
hoods.vibe: A favourite of Tokyo residents: a lake park, a lively alley of tiny bars, and good local shopping.
hoods.do: Inokashira Park and the swan boats; Ghibli Museum (book months ahead).
hoods.eat: Harmonica Yokochō alley; menchi-katsu from Satou.
hoods.shop: Local boutiques, homeware.
hoods.forHer: Easy park paths.

hoods.name: Shinjuku
hoods.vibe: Neon, the busiest station in the world, and one of Tokyo's best gardens.
hoods.do: Shinjuku Gyoen (closed Mondays), free city views from the Metropolitan Government Building.
hoods.eat: Isetan's food hall, Omoide Yokochō, Golden Gai.
hoods.shop: Isetan for Japanese designers.
hoods.forHer: Station is hard work; use exits carefully and taxis.

hoods.name: Azabudai Hills & Roppongi
hoods.vibe: Newer towers with the art museums and immersive digital art.
hoods.do: teamLab Borderless (Azabudai Hills), Mori Art Museum, Roppongi Hills Keyakizaka illumination.
hoods.eat: Food halls in Azabudai Hills.
hoods.shop: Azabudai Hills and Roppongi Hills shops.
hoods.forHer: Indoor, lifts everywhere. teamLab has some dark rooms and slopes.

hoods.name: Takanawa Gateway City
hoods.vibe: A new district built around Takanawa Gateway Station, with the MoN Takanawa museum (opened 28 Mar 2026).
hoods.do: MoN Takanawa: Museum of Narratives, new shops and restaurants.
hoods.eat: New restaurant floors.
hoods.shop: New retail.
hoods.forHer: All new, step-free.

hoods.name: Toyosu
hoods.vibe: The wholesale fish market, and next to it an Edo-style food village with a hot-spring spa.
hoods.do: Tuna auction gallery; Senkyaku Banrai food village, which stays open when the market is closed; rooftop foot bath with bay views.
hoods.eat: Market restaurants from dawn.
hoods.shop: Kitchen and food souvenirs.
hoods.forHer: The foot bath is a good rest stop for her.

hoods.name: Shibamata
hoods.vibe: A slow old temple town on the edge of Tokyo that feels decades behind the centre.
hoods.do: Taishakuten temple and its carved wooden panels, Yamamoto-tei house and garden, Yagiri ferry across the Edo River.
hoods.eat: Kusa-dango (mugwort rice dumplings), eel.
hoods.shop: Old sweet shops and toys.
hoods.forHer: Flat and quiet.

hoods.name: Kagurazaka
hoods.vibe: A former geisha district with stone-paved lanes and small restaurants.
hoods.do: Akagi Shrine, the back lanes off the main slope, Bishamonten temple.
hoods.eat: Kaiseki, French-Japanese bistros, old sweet shops.
hoods.shop: Small craft shops.
hoods.forHer: The main street is a slope; the lanes are flat.

hoods.name: Gōtokuji & Setagaya
hoods.vibe: The temple with hundreds of beckoning-cat figures, and a small tram line through quiet neighbourhoods.
hoods.do: Gōtokuji temple; the Setagaya Line tram.
hoods.eat: Neighbourhood cafés.
hoods.shop: Lucky-cat figures.
hoods.forHer: Flat.

hoods.name: Sunamachi Ginza
hoods.vibe: A 670-metre shopping street where locals buy daily food. No tourists, great snacks.
hoods.do: Walk the street end to end.
hoods.eat: Oden, yakitori, croquettes, rice crackers, all from small shops.
hoods.shop: Everyday Tokyo shopping.
hoods.forHer: Flat.

hoods.name: Parks and gardens
hoods.vibe: Winter is clear and cold, with good light for gardens.
hoods.do: Rikugien and Koishikawa Kōrakuen (classic Edo gardens), Hama-rikyū, Kiyosumi, Shinjuku Gyoen, Inokashira, Yoyogi.
hoods.eat: Teahouses in Hama-rikyū and Rikugien.
hoods.forHer: All have flat paths and benches.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: Higashiyama: temples, old lanes and Gion at night
days.summary: The classic first day. Kiyomizu-dera and the stone-paved lanes below it in the morning, a quiet break, then Gion and a Pontochō dinner as the lanterns come on.

slots.title: Kiyomizu-dera
slots.text: Arrive at opening to get the wooden stage and valley view without the crowds. Steep approach street, some stairs inside the temple grounds.

slots.title: Sannen-zaka & Ninen-zaka
slots.text: Stone-paved lanes lined with old shops, sweets and pottery. Slopes and shallow steps throughout.

slots.title: Kōdai-ji and Ishibe-kōji
slots.text: A quieter temple garden, and the small stone lane behind it that feels like a film set. Good photo stop.

slots.title: Lunch: kaiseki at lunch prices
slots.text: Several kaiseki restaurants around Higashiyama offer a lunch course at roughly half the dinner price. Book ahead for six.

slots.title: Rest
slots.text: Back to the flat, or a long coffee stop.

slots.title: Yasaka Shrine and Maruyama Park
slots.text: Flat approach from Gion. The park behind it is a pleasant, quiet walk.

slots.title: Gion, respectfully
slots.text: Walk Hanami-kōji at dusk. Don't photograph geisha or maiko on the small side streets — it's a ¥10,000 fine — and ask before photographing anyone directly, even on the main street.

slots.title: Dinner in Pontochō
slots.text: A narrow lantern-lit alley of restaurants along the river. Book ahead; most seat small groups. Ask for a riverside kawadoko table if the season allows.

days.label: Day 2
days.title: Arashiyama and the northwest
days.summary: The bamboo grove before the tour buses arrive, a riverside temple garden, then two of Kyoto's most famous northern sights in the afternoon.

slots.title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
slots.text: Arrive before 9:00 for empty photos; it's a short, flat, five-minute walk that gets very crowded by mid-morning.

slots.title: Tenryū-ji garden
slots.text: A Zen garden built around a pond, right at the bamboo grove's entrance. Flat gravel paths, benches throughout.

slots.title: Riverside walk to Togetsukyō Bridge
slots.text: A flat walk along the Katsura River. Rent a rowboat if the group wants, or just enjoy the mountain backdrop.
slots.alt: Optional: the Iwatayama monkey park across the bridge involves a steep 20-minute climb.

slots.title: Sagano Toriimoto
slots.text: A quieter thatched-roof street past the bamboo grove, with far fewer visitors.

slots.title: Lunch: yudōfu in Arashiyama
slots.text: Simmered tofu hotpot, a Kyoto specialty, often served in a temple garden setting. Fully cooked and vegetarian.

slots.title: Rest or travel to the north
slots.text: Arashiyama to Kinkaku-ji is about 30 minutes by bus or taxi.

slots.title: Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion
slots.text: A single loop path around the pond, flat and short but often busy. Photos, not lingering.

slots.title: Ryōan-ji rock garden
slots.text: The famous 15-stone Zen garden, viewed seated from a wooden veranda. Calm and a good rest stop.

slots.title: Dinner downtown
slots.text: Back to Kiyamachi or Shijō for dinner; taxis for six from the north side of the city.

days.label: Day 3
days.title: Fushimi Inari at sunrise, then the market and downtown
days.summary: The famous torii gates before the crowds, a morning at Nishiki Market, and an afternoon in the covered shopping arcades and Nijō Castle.

slots.title: Fushimi Inari-taisha
slots.text: Go before 8:00; crowds build fast from 9:00 and peak 11:00–15:00. Most visitors turn back after 30–45 minutes at the Yotsutsuji viewpoint — go that far for the view over Kyoto, then decide whether to continue.

slots.title: Everyone: breakfast near the shrine or downtown
slots.text: Coffee and a light breakfast, either near the shrine or after the train back downtown.

slots.title: Nishiki Market
slots.text: Kyoto's covered food market: pickles, skewers, sweets, knives and tea. Late December (27–30 Dec) is packed with locals buying New Year food. Some stalls close 31 Dec–3 Jan.

slots.title: Teramachi and Shinkyōgoku arcades
slots.text: Covered shopping streets just off the market for souvenirs, stationery and pottery.

slots.title: Lunch downtown
slots.text: Plenty of counter seating around the market and arcades.

slots.title: Nijō Castle
slots.text: A shogun's palace with famous 'nightingale floors' that chirp as you walk. Flat grounds, some stairs. Usually closed through the New Year holiday — check the dates.

slots.title: Dinner: obanzai counter
slots.text: Kyoto's home-style small dishes, cooked, served one at a time. Calmer than an izakaya, good for a mixed group.

days.label: Day 4
days.title: Philosopher's Path and a hidden-gem afternoon (bonus day)
days.summary: Only if your route gives you a fourth full day, as Route A's does. A flat canal walk between two temples in the morning, then a choice: the tea town of Uji or the quiet valley of Ōhara.

slots.title: Nanzenji and its brick aqueduct
slots.text: A grand temple with a Roman-style brick aqueduct running through the grounds. Some stone steps.

slots.title: Philosopher's Path
slots.text: A flat, canal-side walking path lined with cherry trees, connecting Nanzenji to Ginkaku-ji. About 2 km, 40 minutes at an easy pace, cafés along the way.

slots.title: Hōnen-in
slots.text: A free, mossy, little-visited temple just off the path. Flat approach, a real quiet moment.

slots.title: Ginkaku-ji, the Silver Pavilion
slots.text: A raked-sand garden and a quieter counterpart to Kinkaku-ji. Some gravel paths and a short hillside loop.

slots.title: Lunch nearby, then choose
slots.text: Split here depending on energy and interest.

slots.title: Option A: Uji day trip
slots.text: 30 minutes by train. Byōdō-in temple (on the 10-yen coin) and the birthplace of Japanese green tea. Flat, calm, good matcha sweets.
slots.alt: Option B: Ōhara, a rural valley with Sanzen-in temple's mossy garden — 40 minutes by bus, very few tourists.

slots.title: Farewell dinner
slots.text: Back downtown for a last Kyoto dinner, Pontochō or Kiyamachi.

nights.name: Pontochō
nights.text: A narrow lantern-lit alley along the river, Kyoto's best-known dining street. Small restaurants and bars; reserve for six.

nights.name: Kiyamachi-dōri
nights.text: A canal-side street parallel to Pontochō, more relaxed and easier to walk into without a booking.

nights.name: Gion's Hanami-kōji
nights.text: Kyoto's most traditional dinner setting, best for one splurge night with your parents. Book weeks ahead.

nights.name: Fushimi sake district
nights.text: A canal-side district south of the centre with historic sake breweries. Tastings at Gekkeikan's museum; better as a late-afternoon stop than a night out.

nights.name: Nishiki-kōji in the evening
nights.text: Most food stalls close by early evening, leaving a quiet covered street for a slow walk.

hoods.name: Higashiyama
hoods.vibe: Kyoto's most atmospheric district: Kiyomizu-dera above stone-paved lanes lined with shops from another century.
hoods.do: Kiyomizu-dera, Sannen-zaka and Ninen-zaka, Kōdai-ji, Ishibe-kōji lane, Yasaka Shrine.
hoods.eat: Kaiseki lunch, matcha sweets, yatsuhashi (cinnamon rice cakes).
hoods.shop: Kiyomizu-yaki pottery around Gojō-zaka, tenugui towels, folding fans.
hoods.forHer: Slopes and shallow stone steps throughout; crowded by mid-morning.

hoods.name: Gion & Pontochō
hoods.vibe: The wooden teahouse streets where geisha and maiko still work, and Kyoto's main dining alley along the river.
hoods.do: Hanami-kōji street, Shirakawa canal lane, Yasaka Shrine, Gion Corner for a taste of traditional arts.
hoods.eat: Pontochō and Kiyamachi restaurants, a kaiseki dinner.
hoods.shop: Small craft shops on Shirakawa-dōri.
hoods.forHer: Flat, easy walking. Photography of geisha is banned on the private side streets — ¥10,000 fine.

hoods.name: Arashiyama & Sagano
hoods.vibe: A river valley on Kyoto's edge with the famous bamboo grove, temple gardens, and a quieter preserved street beyond it.
hoods.do: Bamboo Grove (before 9am), Tenryū-ji garden, Togetsukyō Bridge, Sagano Toriimoto preserved street.
hoods.eat: Yudōfu (tofu hotpot) restaurants in temple gardens.
hoods.shop: Small craft and tea shops near the station.
hoods.forHer: Flat throughout; very crowded by mid-morning, calm at dawn.

hoods.name: Fushimi Inari & Fushimi
hoods.vibe: The mountain of a thousand orange gates, and beyond it a quiet canal town of historic sake breweries.
hoods.do: Fushimi Inari-taisha (arrive by 7:00), Gekkeikan sake museum, the Fushimi canal boat ride.
hoods.eat: Sake tastings, simple riverside cafés.
hoods.shop: Sake and sake-related gifts.
hoods.forHer: The lower gates are flat; the full loop is 2–3 hours of stairs and slopes. Very crowded during New Year hatsumōde.

hoods.name: Downtown (Shijō–Kawaramachi)
hoods.vibe: Kyoto's covered food market and its old shopping arcades, all walkable from most machiya stays.
hoods.do: Nishiki Market, Teramachi and Shinkyōgoku arcades, Nijō Castle (10 minutes by bus).
hoods.eat: Market snacks, department store food halls, obanzai counters.
hoods.shop: Ichizawa Shinzaburō canvas bags, Shoyeido incense, SOU•SOU (a Kyoto-founded fashion label), Kyoto Handicraft Center.
hoods.forHer: Flat and easy, with plenty of seating and toilets.

hoods.name: Northwest: Kinkaku-ji & Ryōan-ji
hoods.vibe: Two of Kyoto's most famous gardens, best combined with the Arashiyama day since they're on the same side of the city.
hoods.do: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion), Ryōan-ji's 15-stone rock garden, Ninna-ji.
hoods.eat: Simple noodle shops near the temples.
hoods.shop: Temple charms and incense.
hoods.forHer: Short, flat loop paths; Ryōan-ji has seated veranda viewing.

hoods.name: Philosopher's Path & Nanzenji
hoods.vibe: A flat, tree-lined canal path linking two major temples, with a free hidden-gem temple along the way.
hoods.do: Nanzenji and its brick aqueduct, the Philosopher's Path, Hōnen-in, Ginkaku-ji.
hoods.eat: Small cafés along the path.
hoods.shop: A few craft shops near Ginkaku-ji.
hoods.forHer: Flat path, about 2 km; the easiest full morning in Kyoto for tired legs.

hoods.name: Uji
hoods.vibe: The birthplace of Japanese green tea, 30 minutes from central Kyoto by train.
hoods.do: Byōdō-in temple (the building on the 10-yen coin), tea-ceremony experiences, riverside walks.
hoods.eat: The best matcha desserts in the region.
hoods.shop: Uji-cha (tea) shops.
hoods.forHer: Flat and quiet.

hoods.name: Ōhara
hoods.vibe: A farming valley 40 minutes north of the city, with one of Kyoto's most peaceful moss gardens and almost no tourists.
hoods.do: Sanzen-in temple's moss garden, a walk through the valley's rice fields and pickle shops.
hoods.eat: Local pickles and soba.
hoods.shop: Shiba-zuke pickles, a valley speciality.
hoods.forHer: Some garden paths have steps; the village itself is flat.

hoods.name: Kurama & Kibune
hoods.area: North, day trip · mountain and onsen
hoods.vibe: A wooded mountain temple and a hot spring village in the next valley, connected by a forest hiking trail.
hoods.do: Kurama-dera temple, Kurama Onsen (open-air bath with mountain views), the trail over to Kibune.
hoods.eat: Kibune's famous riverside dining platforms close for winter, but its restaurants stay open indoors.
hoods.forHer: The Kurama–Kibune trail is a real hike with roots and steps; take the train to whichever side you want if energy is short.

hoods.name: Kyoto Station area & Tō-ji
hoods.area: South · practical and one great pagoda
hoods.vibe: Not a place to linger, but Tō-ji's five-storey pagoda, Japan's tallest wooden tower, is worth the stop on the way through.
hoods.do: Tō-ji temple and pagoda, the Kyoto Tower observation deck, the station's own shopping and food floors.
hoods.eat: Station department store food halls.
hoods.shop: Isetan Kyoto, station gift shops for last-minute souvenirs.
hoods.forHer: All flat and step-free.
